title: Exact Hausdorff dimension of Liouville quantum gravity
exact_target: For each fixed gamma in (0,2), compute the deterministic Hausdorff dimension d_gamma of (C,D_h), where h is the whole-plane GFF normalized to have unit-circle average zero and D_h is the canonical gamma-LQG length metric, defined up to deterministic positive multiplication. The general exact function of gamma is requested; the established gamma=sqrt(8/3) case gives d_gamma=4.

primary_sources.verified_content: The median unit-square crossing normalization is a_epsilon=epsilon^(1-xi*Q(xi)+o(1)); Q(gamma/d_gamma)=2/gamma+gamma/2. Problem 5.1 requests d_gamma and the relation between Q and xi. The metric is a length space with locality, pathwise Weyl scaling and affine coordinate covariance.

primary_sources.title: KPZ formulas for the Liouville quantum gravity metric
primary_sources.verified_content: For each alpha in [-2,2], the metric thick-point dimension profile for a deterministic or field-independent random Borel set uses the already implicit coefficient xi=gamma/d_gamma. For a set of Euclidean dimension 2, its profile is (2-alpha^2/2)/(xi*(Q-alpha)). Independence is required for that source theorem; our algebraic identity itself is deterministic.

primary_sources.title: The fractal dimension of Liouville quantum gravity: universality, monotonicity, and bounds
primary_sources.verified_content: For sufficiently small positive gamma, d_gamma >= 2+c*gamma^(4/3)/log(1/gamma) for a universal c>0. This contradicts the O(gamma^2) correction of the Watabiki prediction for sufficiently small gamma; it does not disprove every alternative formula or resolve general d_gamma.
